title: Reverse a String
question: Implement reverseString(str) that returns the string reversed. reverseString('hello') -> 'olleh'.
constraints: Return a new string; handle single-char and empty strings.
hints: A string can be turned into an array with split('').
Array has a reverse() method; join('') turns it back into a string.
bruteForce: Loop from the end building a new string.

discussion.mistakes: Forgetting strings are immutable; off-by-one in manual loops.
followUps: How would you reverse in place if it were an array?
What about Unicode surrogate pairs?

title: Sum an Array
question: Implement sumArray(arr) that returns the sum of all numbers. sumArray([]) must return 0.
hints: reduce takes a callback and an initial accumulator.
Pass 0 as the initial value so an empty array returns 0.
bruteForce: A for loop accumulating into a variable.

discussion.whyAsked: Tests reduce and the importance of the initial value.
discussion.mistakes: Omitting the initial value (breaks on empty arrays).
followUps: Why provide the initial value to reduce?

title: Palindrome Check
question: Implement isPalindrome(str) returning true if the string reads the same forwards and backwards.
hints: Reverse the string and compare to the original.
For a tougher version, ignore case and non-letters.
bruteForce: Two pointers from both ends moving inward.

followUps: Make it ignore spaces, case, and punctuation.
Solve it with O(1) extra space.

title: Count Vowels
question: Implement countVowels(str) that returns how many vowels (a, e, i, o, u) the string contains, case-insensitive.
hints: Lowercase the string first.
Check membership against 'aeiou' or use a regex match.

followUps: Do it with a regex.
Count each vowel's frequency in an object.

title: Remove Duplicates
question: Implement unique(arr) that returns a new array with duplicates removed, preserving first occurrence.
constraints: Return a new array; preserve order of first occurrence.
hints: A Set stores only unique values.
Spread a Set back into an array with [...set].
bruteForce: Nested loop / indexOf check is O(n^2).

discussion.whyAsked: Tests Set knowledge and dedup patterns.
discussion.mistakes: O(n^2) indexOf approach; mutating the input.
followUps: How would you dedup an array of objects by a key?

title: Find the Maximum
question: Implement maxValue(arr) that returns the largest number in the array (works with negatives).
constraints: Handle negative numbers; assume non-empty input.
hints: Math.max(...arr) spreads the array as arguments.
Or reduce keeping the larger of acc and current.
optimized: Math.max(...arr) — but beware very large arrays (call-stack arg limits).

discussion.mistakes: Initializing max to 0 (breaks for all-negative arrays).
followUps: Why is Math.max(...arr) risky for huge arrays?
Solve with reduce.

title: Machine Coding: Implement debounce
question: Implement debounce(fn, delay). It returns a function that delays calling fn until `delay` ms have passed since the last call. Rapid calls should collapse into a single call.
exampleOutput: f runs once, ~50ms after the last call
constraints: Declare it as `function debounce(...)`. Preserve `this` and arguments.
hints: Keep a timer id in a closure.
clearTimeout the previous timer on every call.
Use fn.apply(this, args) to preserve context.
bruteForce: Call fn on every invocation (no debouncing).
optimized: Reset a single timer on each call so only the last one fires.

discussion.whyAsked: The canonical closures + timers machine-coding question.
discussion.mistakes: Losing `this`/args; creating a new timer without clearing the old one.
followUps: Add a leading-edge (immediate) option.
Add a cancel() method.
How does this differ from throttle?

title: Machine Coding: Implement throttle
question: Implement throttle(fn, limit). It returns a function that calls fn at most once per `limit` ms, no matter how often it is invoked.
exampleOutput: f runs once now, then at most once per 100ms
constraints: Declare it as `function throttle(...)`. At most one call per window.
hints: Track the timestamp of the last allowed call.
Compare Date.now() - last against limit.
Preserve `this` and arguments with apply.
optimized: Gate calls by elapsed time since the last run (leading edge).

discussion.whyAsked: Tests rate-limiting logic and the throttle-vs-debounce distinction.
discussion.mistakes: Confusing throttle with debounce; not handling a trailing call.
followUps: Add a trailing-edge call.
When would you throttle vs debounce a scroll handler?

title: Machine Coding: Implement Promise.all
question: Implement promiseAll(promises): return a Promise that resolves to an array of results in input order once all resolve, and rejects as soon as any one rejects.
constraints: Preserve input order even if promises settle out of order. Reject on first rejection.
hints: Return a new Promise.
Store each result at its own index, not by push().
Track a counter; resolve when it equals promises.length.
Wrap items in Promise.resolve() to allow non-promise values.
bruteForce: await each sequentially (loses concurrency and order guarantees).
optimized: Fire all in parallel; place results by index; resolve on the final settle.

discussion.whyAsked: Tests deep Promise understanding: ordering, concurrency, and error propagation.
discussion.mistakes: Using push() (wrong order); forgetting the empty-array case; not handling non-promise values.
followUps: Implement Promise.allSettled.
Implement Promise.race.
How would you add a concurrency limit?

title: Machine Coding: Implement curry
question: Implement curry(fn) so a fixed-arity function can be called with arguments one at a time or in groups: curry(f)(1)(2)(3), curry(f)(1,2)(3), and curry(f)(1)(2,3) all work.
constraints: Use fn.length to know when enough args have arrived.
hints: Collect args; if you have >= fn.length, call fn.
Otherwise return a function that collects more.
Concatenate previously-collected args with new ones.

title: Machine Coding: Deep flatten
question: Implement flatten(arr) that deeply flattens an arbitrarily nested array into a single flat array.
hints: Reduce over the array.
If an element is an array, recurse; otherwise concat it.
Array.isArray tells you which branch.

followUps: Do it iteratively with a stack.
Add a depth limit argument like Array.prototype.flat(depth).

title: Machine Coding: Promise.allSettled
question: Implement promiseAllSettled(promises): resolve to an array of {status:'fulfilled',value} or {status:'rejected',reason} — never reject.
constraints: Must never reject; preserve input order.
hints: Map each promise to one that always resolves to a result object.
Wrap in Promise.resolve to accept non-promises.
Then Promise.all the mapped array.

followUps: How does this differ from Promise.all?
Add a concurrency limit.
